Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:10:1.hebrew: ופרכינן: ואי משתכחי, מי מזבנינן להו? בתמיה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:10:1.english: And we raise an objection: And if they are found, do we sell them? [This is asked] in astonishment:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:10:2.english: Let us be concerned that perhaps he rendered them, etc. - And [thus] the seller ends up feeding terumah to non-priests.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:10:3.hebrew: בדמי תרומה - בזול, שאין עליה קופצין לקנותה, שאינה נאכלת אלא לכהנים וצריכה שימור בטהרה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:10:3.english: At the price of terumah - Cheaply, for there are no [buyers] jumping to purchase it, since it may only be eaten by priests and requires guarding in [a state of] ritual purity.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:11:1.english: It is later on that it becomes greater than their [standard] rate of deterioration - After a long time, their loss is greater than their [standard] rate of deterioration.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:11:2.english: Before it became, etc. - For a person does not leave untithed produce for such a long time as this without fixing [i.e., tithing] them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:13:1.hebrew: והדביש - יצא טעם דובשנו והחמיץ, אשמלי"ר בלע"ז. (כדאתמר) (איוב ל״א:י״ב) "ובכל תבואתי תשרש" — תעקר שרשיה; וכמו "עד לא ירתק חבל הכסף" (קהלת י״ב:ו׳) — יפתחו רתוקות עבותיה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:13:1.english: And it spoiled [vehidbish] - The taste of its honey left [it] and it soured, esmeler in the vernacular [Old French]. (As it is said) (Job 31:12) "And in all my produce it shall be uprooted [tesharesh]" — [meaning] its roots shall be uprooted; and similarly, "before the silver cord is snapped [yeratek]" (Ecclesiastes 12:6) — [meaning] the chains of its cords shall be untied.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:13:2.hebrew: עושה להם תקנה - לקמיה מפרש מאי תקנה יש עוד, הלא כל קילקול העתיד לבא כבר בא הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:13:2.english: He effects a remedy for them - Later [the Gemara] explains what remedy there still is — for has not all the spoilage destined to come already come?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:13:3.english: And he does not sell them to himself - So that they will not suspect him that perhaps he bought them cheaply.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:14:1.english: They change - They exchange copper perutot for silver sela coins, because the perutot corrode and become invalid.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:14:2.english: [Charity] plate - Food that they collect from householders to distribute to the poor every day.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:15:1.hebrew: מאי לאו אפילו יתר מכדי חסרונן - ואיכא למאן דאמר לא יגע, ואת אמרת דברי הכל מוכרן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:15:1.english: What, is it not even more than their [standard] rate of deterioration - And there is one who says he may not touch [them], yet you said all agree he sells them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:15:2.hebrew: אבל אם אבודין יותר מכדי חסרונן - אפילו רבנן מודו דימכרם בב"ד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:15:2.english: But if they are spoiling more than their [standard] rate of deterioration - even the Rabbis agree that he should sell them in court.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:15:3.hebrew: כיון דקם קם - מאחר שעמדו בקלקולם, הרי כבר עמדו ולא יתקלקלו מעתה יותר, אבל שאר פירות הולכין ומרקיבין תמיד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:15:3.english: Once it has stood, it has stood - Once they have settled in their spoiled state, behold they have already stopped [deteriorating] and will not spoil further from now on, whereas other produce goes on rotting continuously.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:1:1.hebrew: והא טעמא דרבי יוסי משום הפסד הרמאי הוא - וכיון דטעמא בהכי, מה לי כלי, מה לי מעות? והיכי תיסק אדעתין למימר דבמעות מודה להו לרבנן, ואמאי אצטריך למתנייה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:1:1.english: But isn't the reason of Rabbi Yosei due to the loss of the fraud - And since the reason lies in this, what [difference is it] to me [whether it is] a vessel, [and] what [difference is it] to me [whether it is] money? And how could it enter our minds to say that regarding money he concedes to the Rabbis, and why was it necessary to teach it?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:1:2.hebrew: לרבנן איצטריך - לאשמועינן מילתא דרבנן תננהו לתרוייהו. ואי תנא כלים ברישא, הכי נמי דלא אצטריך תו למתני מעות; אבל השתא דתני מעות ברישא, תני כלים למימר, לא זו בלבד דליכא פסידא דשבירת כלי, אלא אף זו דאיכא פסידא דגדול, אמרינן הכי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:1:2.english: It is necessary for the Rabbis - To teach us the ruling of the Rabbis, [the Mishnah] taught both of them. And if [the tanna] had taught [the case of] utensils first, indeed there would no longer have been a need to teach [the case of] money; however, now that he teaches [the case of] money first, he teaches [the case of] utensils to say: Not only [in] this [case], where there is no loss of breaking a utensil, but even [in] this [case], where there is a great loss, we say so.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:2:1.hebrew: אבודין - ע"י עכברים או ריקבון:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:2:2.hebrew: לא יגע בהן - למוכרן, וטעמא מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:2:2.english: He may not touch them - to sell them, and the reason is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:3:1.hebrew: קב שלו - חביבה עליו על ידי שעמל בהן, וקב שישאר לו מהם הוא רוצה מתשעה קבין של אחרים שיקח בדמיהן אם ימכרם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:3:1.english: His kav - It is dear to him because he toiled over them, and he prefers a kav that will remain for him from them over nine kav of others that he would buy with their proceeds if he sells them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:3:2.english: We are concerned, etc. - And it is forbidden to feed it to non-priests.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:4:1.hebrew: לפיכך - הואיל ואסור למוכרן משום דרוצה אדם בקב שלו, הרי הן בחזקת קיימים, ומותר בעל הבית לעשותן תרומה ומעשר על פירות שיש לו בביתו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:4:1.english: Therefore - Since it is forbidden [for the bailee] to sell them because a person prefers his own kav, they are presumed to be extant, and the owner is permitted to designate them as terumah and tithe for produce that he has in his house.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:5:1.hebrew: מאי לפיכך - איסור מכירה משום הא הוא, והיכי תלי תנא עשייתו באיסור מכירה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:5:1.english: What [is the meaning of] "therefore"? - The prohibition against selling is because of this, so how does the Tanna make his designating [them as terumah and tithe] dependent on the prohibition against selling?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:5:2.hebrew: השתא דאמור רבנן לא תזבין דחיישינן - שמא עשאן המפקיד תרומה, הרי הן בחזקת שלא נמכרו, ועושה אותן בעל הבית כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:5:2.english: Now that the Sages said, "Do not sell," for we are concerned - lest the depositor made them terumah, they are presumed not to have been sold, and the owner makes them [terumah and tithe], etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:6:2.hebrew: בכדי חסרונן - כדרך שאר תבואות, כמו שמפורש במשנתינו (לקמן בבא מציעא דף מ.) — לחיטין ולאורז תשעה חצאי קבין לכור:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:6:2.english: At their [standard] rate of deterioration - In the manner of other grains, as is stated explicitly in our Mishnah (below, Bava Metzia 40a): for wheat and for rice, nine half-kabs per kor.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:6:3.hebrew: אבל אם אבודין יותר מכדי חסרונן - אפילו רבנן מודו דימכרם בב"ד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:6:3.english: But if they are perishing more than their [standard] rate of deterioration - Even the Rabbis agree that he should sell them in court.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:7:1.hebrew: ודאי פליגא - הא דרבי יוחנן, דאי איכא למיחש לשמא עשאן בעליהן תרומה, אפילו ביותר מכדי חסרונן נמי אסור למזבנינהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:7:1.english: [It] certainly disagrees - This [statement] of Rabbi Yochanan [disagrees with Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak], for if there is [reason] to be concerned lest their owner made them terumah, even [where they deteriorate] more than their [standard] measure of loss it is also forbidden to sell them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:7:2.hebrew: מי לימא פליגא - דוקא אמר רב כהנא, שאם תשעה קבין הן, נוח לו שיאבדו עד קב ואל ימכרם, דהוה ליה יותר מכדי חסרונן, ופליגא הא דר' יוחנן עליה? או לאו דוקא ט' קבין נקט, אלא נוח לו שיהא נפסד קצת, ולעולם כדי חסרונן ותו לא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:7:2.english: Shall we say [that he] disagrees - Did Rav Kahana mean [this] literally — that if there are nine kavs, it is preferable to him that they be lost down to one kav rather than sell them, which would be more than their [normal] rate of deterioration, and [thus] this [statement] of Rabbi Yochanan disagrees with him? Or did he not literally mean nine kavs, rather [he meant] that it is preferable to him that it suffer a slight loss, and in fact [only] up to their [normal] rate of deterioration and no more?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:9:1.english: They raise an objection - Against Rabbi Yochanan.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:9:2.hebrew: וקאכיל - בעל הבית טבלים, שאין פירותיו מתוקנין, שאין אלו קיימין שהוא סומך עליהן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:9:2.english: And he eats - The owner [eats] untithed produce, for his produce is not tithed, since these [fruits] upon which he relies are not extant.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 38a:9:3.english: [They are] uncommon - And one need not be concerned about this.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 38a:11:1.hebrew: מזבנינן לכהנים - ולשמא יעשם אחר המכירה ליכא למיחש, דיתר מכדי חסרונן לא שכיח, וכי עביד להו בעה"ב תרומה ומעשר, עביד להו מקמי דליהוו יותר מכדי חסרונן. ופריך: לרב נחמן נמי דלזבנינהו לכהנים! בכדי חסרונן לא פריך, דהא איכא למיחש לשמא יעשם, אלא ביותר מכדי חסרונם פריך דלזבנינהו; וכי תימא הכי נמי — והא אמרת דרב נחמן ודאי פליג! ומשני דלרב נחמן יותר מכדי חסרונן שכיח. והקשה ריב"ם: מי דחקו לומר דרב נחמן פליג? לימא דביתר מכדי חסרונן לד"ה מוכרן, וליכא למיחש לשמא יעשם, דלא שכיח, כמו לרב כהנא? ותי' ר"ת: דמתני' מיירי אפילו בפשתן או בפירות מתוקנים, והתם מאי טעמא לא יגע בהם? ע"כ משום דרב כהנא, דרוצה אדם בקב שלו מבתשעה קבין של חבירו. אם כן, מאי אהני טעמא דשמא עשאן תרומה ומעשר על מקום אחר, אי לאו לאשמועינן דאפי' ביתר מכדי חסרונן חיישינן? א"כ, סבר דאפילו יותר מכדי חסרונן שכיח:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 38a:11:1.english: We sell [them] to priests - And regarding [the concern that] perhaps he will make them [terumah] after the sale, there is no need to be concerned, because [deterioration] greater than their [standard] rate of deterioration is not common, and when the owner makes them terumah and tithe, he makes them [so] before they reach [deterioration] greater than their [standard] rate of deterioration. And [the Gemara] asks: According to Rav Naḥman as well, let him sell them to priests! [Regarding deterioration] within their [standard] rate of deterioration it does not ask [this], for there is reason to be concerned that perhaps he will make them [terumah]; rather, [regarding deterioration] greater than their [standard] rate of deterioration it asks that he should sell them; and if you say that [this is] indeed so — but you said that Rav Naḥman certainly disagrees! And [the Gemara] answers that according to Rav Naḥman, [deterioration] greater than their [standard] rate of deterioration is common. And Rivam asked: What forced him to say that Rav Naḥman disagrees? Let us say that in [a case of deterioration] greater than their [standard] rate of deterioration, according to everyone he sells them, and there is no need to be concerned that perhaps he will make them [terumah], since it is not common, just as according to Rav Kahana? And Rabbeinu Tam answered: The Mishnah deals even with flax or with tithed produce, and there, what is the reason [that] he should not touch them? Perforce [it is] because of Rav Kahana's [reason], that a person prefers his own kav over nine kavin of his fellow's. If so, what did [Rav Naḥman's] reason of "perhaps he made them terumah and tithe for another place" accomplish, if not to teach us that even in [a case of deterioration] greater than their [standard] rate of deterioration we are concerned [about it]? If so, he holds that even [deterioration] greater than their [standard] rate of deterioration is common.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 38a:3:1.hebrew: שמא עשאן תרומה ומעשר על מקום אחר - הקשה ר"ת: וכי נחשדו חבירים לתרום שלא מן המוקף, כדאמר בפרק כל הגט (גיטין דף ל:) ופ"ק דחולין (דף ז.) גבי ר"מ שאכל עלה של ירק? ואור"ת, דהכא גבי פקדון תולין בחששא מועטת שלא יגע בהם, וחיישינן שמא בערב שבת תרם שלא מן המוקף, דשרי, כדאמרינן בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף צג.). אי נמי, כדאמרינן פרק בכל מערבין (עירובין דף לב:): ניחא ליה לחבר דליעביד איסורא זוטא, דהיינו שלא מן המוקף. אבל בחולין (דף ז.) ובפרק כל הגט (גיטין דף ל:) לא חיישינן, כיון שאינו פקדון. וטפי אמרינן בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף ל.): ראו שאביהם הטמין מעות בשידה, תיבה ומגדל ואמר "של מעשר שני הם", אם כמערים — לא אמר כלום; אלמא אזלינן בתר רוב מעות שהם חולין להקל, ואע"פ שפירש שהם מעשר. ובהאשה שהלכה (יבמות דף קטו:) גבי מצא כלי והיה כתוב עליו קו"ף — קרבן, תי"ו — תרומה, הא אין כתוב עליו — לא חיישינן. והא דאמרינן בהזהב (לקמן בבא מציעא דף מט.): "ישראל שאמר לבן לוי: כור מעשר לאביך בידי — רשאי לעשותו תרומת מעשר על מקום אחר", היינו נמי בשבתות וימים טובים. וכן הא דקתני בסמוך: "לפיכך בעל הבית עושה אותו תרומה ומעשר על מקום אחר":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 38a:3:1.english: Perhaps he rendered them terumah and tithe for another place - Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: Are chaverim [scrupulous individuals] suspected of separating terumah from produce that is not adjacent [to the produce being tithed], as stated in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (Gittin 30b) and the first chapter of Chullin (7a) regarding Rabbi Meir who ate a leaf of a vegetable? And Rabbeinu Tam answered that here, regarding a deposit, we rely even on a slight concern so that he will not touch them, and we are concerned that perhaps on Shabbat eve he separated terumah from produce that was not adjacent, which is permitted, as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaIshah Rabbah (Yevamot 93a). Alternatively, [it is] as we say in the chapter [entitled] BeKol Me'arvin (Eruvin 32b): a chaver prefers to commit a minor prohibition — namely, [separating terumah] from produce that is not adjacent. However, in Chullin (7a) and in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (Gittin 30b), we are not concerned [about this], since it is not a deposit. And even further, we say in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 30a): [If] they saw their father hide money in a chest, box, or cabinet, and he said, "They are [money] of second tithe," if [he said it] as one acting with artifice, he has said nothing; thus, we follow the majority of money, which is non-sacred, to rule leniently, even though he explicitly stated that it is tithe. And in [the chapter entitled] HaIshah SheHalkhah (Yevamot 115b), regarding one who found a vessel and there was written on it [the letter] kof — [it is] korban [consecrated], [the letter] tav — [it is] terumah; thus, [if] it is not written on it, we are not concerned. And that which we say in [the chapter entitled] HaZahav (below, Bava Metzia 49a): "An Israelite who said to a Levite: 'A kor of tithe belonging to your father is in my possession,' [the Levite] is permitted to make it terumat ma'aser [tithe of the tithe] for another place" — that too is [referring to] Sabbaths and festivals. And likewise that which is taught nearby: "Therefore, the owner may make it terumah and tithe for another place."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 38a:6:1.hebrew: מחלוקת בכדי חסרונן - פרש"י: כדרך שאר תבואות. והקשה ריב"ם: וכי פליגי במשהו, דבפחות מכדי חסרונן לכ"ע לא ימכור? ועוד, דא"כ מ"ט דרשב"ג? וי"ל: דפליגי שנתחסר בחדש או בחדשים יותר משרגילות להתחסר עד אותו הזמן, ופליגי עד שיעלה החסרון בחדש או בשני חדשים תשעה חצאי קבין לכור, שהוא בכדי חסרונן לשנה שלימה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 38a:6:1.english: The dispute [is in a case where it deteriorates] at its [standard] rate of deterioration - Rashi explained: [at the rate of deterioration] like other produce. And Rivam raised a difficulty: Do they argue over a minuscule difference — that for [anything] less than the standard rate of deterioration, according to everyone he may not sell [it]? Furthermore, if so, what is the reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel [for permitting him to sell it]? And one can answer: They argue [in a case] where it deteriorated in a month or in two months more than [produce] normally deteriorates up to that time, and they argue [up to the point] until the deterioration in a month or in two months reaches nine half-kabin per kor, which is [the equivalent of] its standard rate of deterioration for a full year.
